clue.text: I am sorry, darling (repeatedly)

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an exclamation of regret

indicators.note: the bracketed word tells the solver to say the term of endearment over again, two copies in a row

parts.note: a darling is a dear, a loved one

explanation.surface: Someone apologises to a loved one, and keeps on apologising.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a mild expression of regret or dismay, the sort of thing said when apologising.

clue.text: Do not slow up or stop working

indicators.note: letters that are up are in a turmoil, stirred up, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction not to slow down, or else to halt work.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who down tools go on strike, an idiom for ceasing work.

clue.text: Shot half-cut emir put in a dry pint

indicators.note: the half emir is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking

indicators.note: the word emir is cut in half, leaving its first two letters

explanation.surface: A tipsy Arab ruler is offered a pint of alcohol-free beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like drunk but halves EMIR to EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to make an attempt or try.

clue.text: Lament bringing up part of crossword, Serpent's fifth

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing a word up reverses it

parts.note: the grid is part of a crossword

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the word Serpent's is picked

explanation.surface: Mourning a crossword clue about a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Foolish: like 1, 3 and 6 collectively

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the Roman numeral for one is I
three and six added together make nine

explanation.surface: Something foolish compared to clues 1, 3 and 6 together.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues, but they are just numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid, from the donkey, a symbol of foolishness.

clue.text: Special Brew drained dry — keep calm

parts.note: a brew is a pot of tea in British usage

indicators.note: a drained word has its contents emptied out, leaving only the outside letters of the word dry

explanation.surface: Someone who has finished off a can of Special Brew strong lager is told to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Special Brew is a notoriously strong British lager, which makes the surface about drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection used to tell someone to stay composed and not get excited, as in 'Steady, now!'

clue.text: To shoot me is wrong, but alluring

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shooting me would be wrong, though tempting.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty, and by extension attractive or sexually appealing.

clue.text: Trouble with stripping amid a crowd

indicators.note: the stripped letters are placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: the gate is the number attending a sports match, a crowd

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer letters, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: Trouble arising when someone takes their clothes off in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or worry them, a verb synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Being blocked by the old lord, I give up

indicators.note: the I is hemmed in by the other letters around it

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A frustrated person, obstructed by an elderly aristocrat, admits defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender or concede, a synonym for give up.

clue.text: Top drugs and crack the old man sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are sent upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them make drugs
a crack at something is a go, an attempt
pa is a word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: Top-quality drugs and crack sent to the old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' suggests cocaine but means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point, the peak or climax of something.

clue.text: @BuckPalBabe after show's end, drink?

indicators.note: the at-sign piece and the royal piece come after the letter taken from show
the end of the word show is its final letter

parts.note: the @ symbol is read as the word at
a cheeky name for the Queen, the 'babe' of Buckingham Palace; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A tweet tagging a royal-themed social media handle, asking whether it fancies a drink after a show.
explanation.walkthrough: '@BuckPalBabe' looks like a social media handle; read the symbol as a word, and 'Buck Pal Babe' as the Buckingham Palace darling, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain water is the most basic drink of all, here the clue's question-marked definition.

clue.text: Better to cover doctrine briefly and wing it

indicators.note: the verb for better goes over the shortened doctrine, holding it inside

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

indicators.note: a word given briefly loses its last letter

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: Advice to improve a policy summary and then just make things up as you go.
explanation.definitionFit: To wing it is an idiom for acting without preparation, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: Floridian city cartel caught messing around

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard, so the phrase is what the ear picks up

parts.note: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida; a ring is a group of traders fixing prices, a cartel

explanation.surface: A drug cartel from a Florida city is arrested while up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like an arrest but signals that TAMPA RING, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampering is interfering with something improperly, a meddling synonym for messing around.

clue.text: Tried brains stuffed with bit of radish?

indicators.note: the word for brains is filled with a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: your head is your brains, your intelligence

indicators.note: a bit of the word radish here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether brains filled with a little radish have been tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' is the legal sense: a court case that has been heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that a court has tried is one the judge has listened to and judged, a legal synonym.

clue.text: Firm punches KO'd Hoskins? Result

indicators.note: the firm abbreviation pushes into the middle of the other pieces, as a punch goes in

parts.note: a boxer who is KO'd, knocked out, is out
Hoskins is the setter, who refers to himself as me
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A boxing report: a company's punches knock out the setter, so what was the result?
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the result or consequence of an event.

clue.text: Stubborn old boy popular in Express

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the popular word is placed inside the verb for express

parts.note: to state something is to express it
something in is popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A stubborn former pupil who is popular on the Express newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person refuses to change their mind, so is stubborn.

clue.text: Couples going off to ring each other?

definitions.text: Couples going off to ring each other?

parts.words: Couples going off to ring each other?
parts.note: pairs who run away to marry secretly, putting wedding rings on each other, rather than phoning

explanation.surface: Couples heading off to telephone one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a phone call, but it is the wedding ring each partner gives the other after running away.
explanation.definitionFit: People who elope run off secretly to get married, exchanging rings.

clue.text: Fancy estate houses I'll flipping moon?

indicators.note: the rearranged estate holds the reversed letters inside it
fancy, as an adjective meaning elaborate, signals the letters of estate are rearranged
the letters of I'll are flipped round, reversed

explanation.surface: Someone at a fancy housing estate swears they'll flipping moon somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges the estate letters to SATETE, which 'houses' the reversed letters; 'moon' looks like a rude verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon is a natural body that orbits a planet, the standard example of one.

clue.text: Appears embarrassed, seeing north as south

indicators.note: the letter standing for north is replaced by the letter standing for south

parts.note: to be shown up is to be embarrassed in public

explanation.surface: Someone looks embarrassed after mixing up their compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to arrive or turn up, a phrasal verb meaning appears.

clue.text: Month with no drink upset army type!

parts.note: Oct is short for October
O is nil, nothing, no

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the drink word over, reversing it

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A soldier upset at going a month without a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army type' looks like a soldier but means a creature with many arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed sea creature is literally arm-y, having lots of arms.

clue.text: No more sex, being thus?

parts.note: something past is over, no more
it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their sex life is over because of their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too old for something is the idiom here, and loss of libido is one sign of ageing.

clue.text: Stylish European support worker

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A smart European who works as a support worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and refined in appearance or manner, a direct synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Aussie's view of male in course became apparent

indicators.note: Australia is down under, so an Aussie sees things upside down; in a down clue that reverses the letters
the male letter is placed inside the course word

parts.note: a degree is a university course

explanation.surface: An Australian's opinion of a man on a university course appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view or become known, so it means became apparent.

clue.text: A couple of grads touring city state

indicators.note: the graduates go around the city, holding its letters inside

parts.note: BA and MA are two university degrees held by graduates
LA is Los Angeles, a city

explanation.surface: Two graduates touring a city in some American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the United States, in the Deep South.

clue.text: African tenor wearing dodgy suit

indicators.note: the tenor wears the suit, so the suit's letters wrap round him
dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters of suit are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: An African tenor singer dressed in a suspect suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges SUIT to TUSI, which goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: US President ignoring you for a floozie

indicators.note: the letter standing for you is left out of the president's name
the new letter is put in the place of the dropped one

parts.note: Donald Trump was a US President
U sounds like and stands for you in texting

explanation.surface: A US President who ignores you in favour of a woman of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is dated slang for a promiscuous woman, a floozie.

clue.text: Dance on amphetamine or mix of coke and H

indicators.note: the dance word goes on after the drug word

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone at a dance high on amphetamine, or on a cocaine-heroin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedball is a drug cocktail of cocaine and heroin; H is slang for heroin.

clue.text: Some cook kedgeree up — or gander

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the hidden letters read upwards, backwards
some of the letters of the phrase cook kedgeree are taken out

explanation.surface: Cooking up a breakfast of kedgeree, or taking a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gander' suggests a goose but means a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a quick look: a dekko or a gander.

clue.text: Write off plain page? Charming!

indicators.note: a written-off car is wrecked, so the letters of these words are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a blank sheet of paper, then sarcastically calls it charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing is attractive or pleasing, a synonym for charming.

clue.text: Two kilos I cut with hot American brown

indicators.note: the pair of kilos and I are cut apart and the other letters slotted in

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilo, so two give KK
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A recipe step: two kilos cut with something hot and American, giving brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow colour, used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Sign that is to say: tartish types crossing

indicators.note: the pastries go across the abbreviation, holding it in their middle

parts.note: pies are things of the tart sort, baked pastry with a filling
SC, short for Latin scilicet, means that is to say

explanation.surface: A sign announces that some tarty women are crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tartish types' suggests loose women but means pastries like tarts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fish is one of the twelve zodiac signs, a star sign.

clue.text: Support briefs with the rear end cut out

indicators.text: with the rear end cut out
indicators.note: the last letter of the word for barristers is removed

parts.note: briefs are barristers, lawyers who are briefed; advocates in court

explanation.surface: Supportive underpants with the back cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to publicly back or recommend it, a verb synonym.
